title: "The dearest land"
hook: leaving, he says to Mecca: you are the dearest land to me, and if your people hadn't driven me out I'd never have left (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday: al-Amin, and Ali returning every trust. Your line was: trusts returned, even then.

The city that just tried to kill him is behind him now. Its leaders mocked him. Its council voted on his death. Its young men waited at his door with swords. And as the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, leaves it, the hadith keep words he speaks to it. Not to the people. To the place itself. Two companions report what he said, and both reports are kept in the collection of al-Tirmidhi. Today: Mecca.
screen: `THE CITY BEHIND HIM.` → `HE SPEAKS TO MECCA.` → `HE SPEAKS TO THE PLACE.`

segments.voice: In one report, from Abdullah ibn Adi, the Prophet stands at a spot in Mecca and says: by God, you are the best of God's earth, and the dearest of God's earth to God. And if I had not been driven out of you, I would never have left. In the other, from Ibn Abbas, he speaks more personally: how good you are as a land, and how dear you are to me. If my people had not driven me out, I would never have lived anywhere but you. Listen to the two halves. The first is pure love: dearest, best, how good you are. The second names what happened, with no softening: I was driven out. He doesn't pretend he's leaving by choice. And he doesn't let what the people did turn into hatred for the place. The Qur'an uses the same plain language: the town that drove you out. Grief and love, and the truth about why, all in two sentences. Anyone who has left a hometown, a country, a house they grew up in, may know the shape of it. You can love a place and still be forced to leave it, and you can say both out loud. Mecca will come back into his life later. Here, he says goodbye.
screen: `THE DEAREST OF GOD'S EARTH.` · `IF I HADN'T BEEN DRIVEN OUT.` · `LOVE AND TRUTH TOGETHER.` · `THE TOWN THAT DROVE YOU OUT.` · then, large: `THE DEAREST LAND.`

segments.voice: Let a place you've left come to you, a childhood home, a city, a room that isn't yours anymore, and walk through it slowly: the light, the smell, who was there. If the reason you left still stings, let it be true without arguing with it, then silently tell the place what it was to you, in one or two plain sentences, the way he did. If you pray, you can thank God for that place.
Mecca. Leaving the city, the Prophet told it he would never have left if he hadn't been driven out, the dearest land to him. Today's word.
Your line: grief and love, both true. Neither one had to cancel the other. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Muslims quote the Prophet's farewell to Mecca when they speak of love for one's homeland, and Mecca remains the city Muslims face in prayer and travel to on pilgrimage.

chat.says: Was the Prophet glad to leave Mecca, after how it treated him?
options: No. He called it the dearest land; he left only because he was driven out.
Yes. He was relieved to get away, and he never spoke of it fondly.
He left angry, and cursed the city on his way out of it.
chat.meaning: In al-Tirmidhi he tells Mecca how dear it is, and that he would never have left if his people hadn't driven him out.

al-Tirmidhi.meaning: compiler of a major collection of the Prophet's sayings

Abdullah ibn Adi.meaning: a companion who reported the farewell to Mecca

Ibn Abbas.meaning: a companion who reported the second version

Mecca.meaning: the Prophet's home city, which drove him out

sources.ref: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3925 (Abdullah ibn Adi ibn al-Hamra: the best and dearest of God's earth; if I had not been driven out I would not have left)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3926 (Ibn Abbas: how good you are as a land and how dear to me; if my people had not driven me out I would not have lived elsewhere)
Qur'an 47:13 (the township which drove you out)

notes: Tirmidhi numbers 3925 and 3926 as recalled; confirm numbering and that both are graded acceptable.
The Abdullah ibn Adi report places the words at al-Hazwara in Mecca, not necessarily on the night of the hijra; the script frames it as said while leaving, following the index. Confirm framing.
'Where he was born, where Khadijah is buried': confirm both are fitting to state here.
'Mecca will come back into his life, years from now' alludes to the later conquest without dating it.
